tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.text:
Run_0703 (old code, before the last-tab fix) finished with **34.3**, signed and eligible. I've added the score to `.swarm/runs/INDEX.md`.

**What it got right:**
- Decision, tender reference and the 5% discount.
- The withdrawn Q&A quantity check.
- Material, quantity and base price on 01.01 and 01.05.

**Where the points went:**
1. **01.02, 01.03 and 01.04 were left out (−39).** Their ERP prices are in USD, and the Devisenfixing (FX) mail was found in the archive but never read, so the agent could not convert them. This is the biggest gap.
2. **Surcharge, packaging, setup and bonus were missing on the two positions it bid.** The mails for packaging rates, metal index, setup pools and project bonus were never read, because the mail browser died at 2:39 and the mail work then shared browser 0 with everything else. That also cost the final unit price, the net total, the arithmetic check and the metal-index check (another ~15).
3. **Both lead times were wrong.** No stock figures were saved for any material, so the agent used production lead times (7 and 12 weeks). Even so, one stock screen did show 99 pieces for HZ-1609, which is more than the 25 needed. The ERP also lost time on 404s from guessed tab addresses.

**Run_d645 (with the fix) so far:**
- The mail browser has survived three hung-tab closes. "Unreachable" has not appeared once, and in 0703 it showed up repeatedly.
- The mail lanes are now saving records; Technikfreigabe came in with 5. This is exactly the failure behind point 2, so d645 should read more of those mails.
- The monitor is still running. I'll report its board summary and score when they arrive.

If d645 confirms the mail browser stays alive, the next fixes in order of payoff are making the FX read reliable (up to +39) and getting the ERP agent to actually save stock figures.

def check(m: dict, req: dict, stroke: Decimal | None, min_known: int = MIN_KNOWN) -> list[str] | None:
    """None if `m` contradicts the requirement or too little of it was read; else the attributes that could not be
    verified (not shown, or the usable-travel reserve unknown)."""
    if sum(not blank(m.get(a)) for a in ("bore", "stroke", "pressure", "mounting", "certification")) < min_known:
        return None
    unverified = []
    for attr, equal in (("bore", same), ("pressure", same), ("mounting", text_equal), ("certification", text_equal)):
        if blank(m.get(attr)):
            unverified.append(attr)
        elif not equal(m.get(attr), req.get(attr)):
            return None
    have = num(m.get("stroke"))
    if have is None:
        unverified.append("stroke")
    elif stroke is not None:
        if have != stroke:
            return None
    else:                                  # usable travel, reserve unknown: nominal stroke must at least cover it
        usable = num(req.get("stroke"))
        if usable is None or have < usable:
            return None
        unverified.append("stroke")
    return unverified


def reserve_fallback(cands: list[dict], req: dict, stroke: Decimal | None) -> dict | None:
    """For a usable-travel requirement whose reserve is unknown: the ONLY active candidate, otherwise verified, whose
    nominal stroke lies above the usable travel (equal = no reserve). Several such candidates: no guess, since the
    reserve decides between them."""
    usable = num(req.get("stroke"))
    if stroke is not None or req.get("stroke_kind") != "usable" or usable is None:
        return None
    fits = [c for c in cands if c["active"] is True and c["unverified"] == ["stroke"]
            and num(c["stroke"]) is not None and num(c["stroke"]) > usable]
    return fits[0] if len(fits) == 1 else None

                    priced=frozenset()) -> dict:
    """`priced`: normalised numbers of materials with a price condition read (preferred among equal candidates)."""
    out = {}
    for p in (tender or {}).get("positions") or []:
        pos = str(p.get("position")).strip()
        ref = next((r for r in requirements if norm_ref(r) == norm_ref(p.get("requirement_ref"))), None)
        req = requirements.get(ref) if ref else None
        if not req:
            out[pos] = {"material": None, "reason": f"requirement {p.get('requirement_ref')} not found",
                        "candidates": [], "unverified": []}
            continue
        stroke = required_stroke(req, mail, current)
        group = norm_ref(req.get("kataloggruppe"))
        cands = []
        for m in materials.values():
            if group and norm_ref(m.get("kataloggruppe")) and norm_ref(m.get("kataloggruppe")) != group:
                continue
            unverified = check(m, req, stroke)
            if unverified is None:
                continue
            active = m.get("is_active")
            cands.append({"material": m["material"], "status": m.get("status_code"), "unverified": unverified,
                          "stroke": m.get("stroke"),
                          "active": True if active in (True, "true") else False if active in (False, "false") else None})
        # best first: active before unknown status, fully verified before unverified, then the shortest fitting stroke
        usable = [c for c in cands if c["active"] is True and not c["unverified"]]
        usable.sort(key=lambda c: (c["active"] is not True, len(c["unverified"]),

        required = {k: req.get(k) for k in ("bore", "pressure", "mounting", "certification", "kataloggruppe")}
        required["stroke"] = None if stroke is None else format(stroke.normalize(), "f")
        if usable:

            out[pos] = {"material": best["material"], "required": required, "candidates": cands, "reason": reason,

    return out

content.text:
Run_d645 is going to score badly, probably around 10. It's signing an empty bid: 5 positions, 0 with a material.

- **What worked:** the mail browser fix. Three hung mail tabs were closed and the browser stayed up the whole run ("unreachable" never appeared). The discount (5%), condition rules, technical release and packaging rates were all read.
- **Why the bid is empty:** all four browsers froze together on their first page, costing about 4½ minutes. The ERP agent only got going at minute 7, after the spec was read. It never reached the material status tab, and the matcher only accepts materials confirmed active. So every position came out "no material".
- **Why FX was missed again:** its search tab hung, and the retry was queued behind the lower-value topics. Collection ended before it ran.

I made four fixes, committed as `41f7fc5` on `kurk-s/mail-topics`. All 183 tests pass, and two of them are new:
1. **Matcher:** when there is exactly one material that matches the spec exactly and its status wasn't read, it now uses it instead of giving up. With two look-alikes it still won't guess, since one is usually the blocked decoy. On d645's data this would have filled about 3 of the 5 positions.
2. **ERP start:** if the first login dies within a step or two at startup, the ERP agent now logs in again right away instead of waiting for the spec.
3. **Mail retry order:** a failed topic is retried ahead of the lower-value topics in its tab, so FX goes before delivery commitments.
4. **FX gap:** the coordinator now asks for the FX mail as soon as it sees a USD price, without waiting for the price table to be read.

The branch is pushed (`f8d2a78`, docs note included) and there's a note for ksiox1337's integration in `docs/INTEGRATION.md`. I'll post d645's final score when it arrives. Once d645 finishes I can start a test run on `41f7fc5` if you want.

content.text:
ksiox's 69 run was on almost the same code as mine. Their `main` already includes everything from my branch, including the last-tab fix. On top of that it has two fixes of theirs I didn't have:

1. **`54fefd1`, guard:** after each mail search our code dragged the gate slider again, which took the cursor out of the search box. That matches the endless slider drags in our mail logs.
2. **`d8bc223`, `read_page`:** it now waits for the mail reading pane to load before saving. Before, the setup-pool, project-bonus and price-index mails were saved as "frame not readable", so those rates were missing from every position.

My 10 came from things those fixes don't cover:
- **Slow start:** all four browsers froze together at the start, so the ERP agent never reached the material status tab.
- **Strict matcher:** it then dropped every material it couldn't confirm as active, so the bid was empty.
- **FX retry order:** the FX search hung and its retry was queued last.

I merged their `main` into `kurk-s/mail-topics` and pushed it as `f07d702`. All 185 tests pass on the merge. The branch is now ksiox's 69 code plus my fixes for those three problems (`41f7fc5`).

I looked at their commits in Git, not at their run's logs. The rules here only let me look at run data you've identified as yours.

The useful next step is a test run of `f07d702`, to check that my fixes add points on top of their 69 and don't lose any. Should I start it, or check with ksiox first that it won't clash with a run they have going?

# Collecting and analysing stop `submit_reserve()` seconds before expiry; the rest belongs to SUBMIT (filling the bid
# form and signing takes several minutes of browser steps). SUBMIT itself stops FINAL_MARGIN_S before expiry.
# signing 4 positions took 466 s in run_7732ba545b50b3a5 and ended 60 s before expiry; a 5th position adds ~90 s.
# SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S > 0 fixes the reserve; by default it is estimated during the run from the positions to enter
# and the measured pace of browsing steps (see Context.submit_reserve), within [MIN_RESERVE_S, MAX_RESERVE_S].
SUBMIT_RESERVE_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S", 0)) or 600     # the upper bound / fixed value
FIXED_RESERVE = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S", 0)) > 0
# Signing took 3:17 to 8:40+ in eight sandbox runs (2026-10-11); with a 444 s reserve run_53e37fff66cc4cc7 ran out of
# time. Until signing is consistently faster the live estimate may save at most 60 s of the 600 s.
MIN_RESERVE_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_MIN_RESERVE_S", 540))
MAX_RESERVE_S = SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
FINAL_MARGIN_S = 40
# Submission model, in browsing steps: wizard steps independent of the positions (login, tender, wizard start, bidder,
# decision, documents, TAN request/entry, summary, confirmation, receipt), steps per position, and the steps the
# wizard warm-up (agents/submit_bid.WizardPrep) already did. Full-reasoning submitter steps are slower than the
# flash steps measured during collection. TAN lookup runs next to the wizard and costs extra time only at the end.
# run_7b060fa870cea9b6: an entered position took 3 steps (one 6: cascading selects), an omitted one 1 step
BASE_STEPS, STEPS_PER_POSITION, PREP_SAVES_STEPS = 12, 3, 4
# Measured submitter pace vs collection pace: run_56cfdff4ff83d569 36 steps / 470 s (13 s), run_7a11d3a90d55e1ce
# 26 steps / 316 s (12 s, collection median ~11-12 s at the time): full-reasoning steps are only slightly slower.
FULL_REASONING_FACTOR, TAN_S, SAFETY_S = 1.15, 60, 45
MIN_SUBMIT_STEP_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_MIN_SUBMIT_STEP_S", 13))   # a submitter step is never assumed faster
# A scored run lasts 20 minutes; test runs may last 2 hours. Every run plans with at most RUN_LIMIT_S from process
# start, so test runs show the timing (and the follow-ups that fit) of a scored run. The run's real expiry still wins
# when it is earlier.
RUN_LIMIT_S = float(os.environ.get("SWARM_RUN_LIMIT_S", 1200))


@dataclass
class Context:
77:    async def browse(self, job: str, **kwargs):
78-        kwargs.setdefault("stop_extra", MAIL_STOP_EXTRA_S)
79-        return await super().browse(job, **kwargs)
80-
81-    def stop_extra(self, kwargs: dict) -> float:
82-        return kwargs.get("stop_extra", MAIL_STOP_EXTRA_S)
83-
    noise without inputs (the bid submitter). `dedupe_reads`: read_page of a URL another agent already saved returns
    the saved text instead of opening it again (off for mails that change, such as TANs). `idle_steps`: after the
    first saved page/fact, stop once this many steps in a row saved nothing new (the caller resumes).
    """
    records: list[dict] = []
    progress = {"saved_at": None, "idle_stop": False}     # step of the last saved page/fact

    def reserve() -> float:
        """Seconds-left mark at which this browse stops: fixed, or the live submission reserve plus `stop_extra`."""
        if stop_reserve is not None:
            return stop_reserve
        return ctx.stop_at(stop_extra) if ctx is not None and hasattr(ctx, "stop_at") else stop_extra

    async def emit(rec: dict) -> None:
        records.append(rec)
        progress["saved_at"] = len(step_started)

content.text:
Run_78a9 is weak too. The board shows a bid with only position 01.01, and the other four were left out. My fixes didn't cause that: browsers kept freezing.

- **The mail browser froze from the start.** It sat 3½ minutes on the login page: its first step hit the 2-minute step timeout, then twice more the page state didn't load in time. Mail work only began at 01:51. Mail stops 150 s before the rest of collection (CRUBSTERINO's setting), so the mail agents had about 4 minutes. Mail ended with 14 pages read and none of the rates that set the price extracted: packaging, metal index, FX and the rest.
- **The ERP agent also stalled.** It logged in cleanly, so my login retry wasn't needed. Then the search window opened in a new tab and twice the page state didn't load in time, costing about a minute per search.
- **My fixes behaved as intended but had no data to work on.** The FX gap now appears as soon as a USD price is seen ("mail fx USD"), but mail had no time left to read the FX mail. The new status-unread fallback didn't need to fire, because positions 01.02–01.04 got materials through the existing rule for an unread end reserve. Their prices were still missing, and that's why they were left out.

ksiox's 69 used nearly the same code, so much of the gap between runs comes from whether the browsers freeze early. That freezing happens at every run's start (0703, d645, 78a9) and is the next thing worth fixing. I'll post the score when it arrives.

content.text:
Run_78a9 failed with a score of 0: it ran out of time before signing, so no bid was submitted. My fixes weren't the cause. This run lost time to browser freezes, slow model replies while filling the bid form, and a slow lookup of the signing code (TAN).

1. **Start (minutes 0–5):** the mail browser stuck on the login page. The first mail page came in only at 333 s. Mail stops 2½ minutes before the rest of collection, so mail had about 4 minutes. The bid ended up with only position 01.01.
2. **Bid form (minutes 11–14):** the first submit attempt hit four 40-second model timeouts on one button for 01.01 and gave up. The second attempt had to start the form from scratch.
3. **Signing (last 3 minutes):** the TAN was requested with 172 s left. The TAN reader opened the inbox before the TAN mail had arrived, then spent 5 steps dragging the search slider. It only saw the TAN after a reload, and time ran out.

I fixed point 3 in `e76aad5`: the TAN reader now reloads an empty inbox instead of fighting the slider. All 185 tests pass, and it's pushed to `kurk-s/mail-topics`. I've added the run to `.swarm/runs/INDEX.md`.

Points 1 and 2 decide most runs now. ksiox's 69 and my 10 and 0 came from almost the same code, so results swing on whether the browsers and the model stall early. More test runs from me mostly measure that luck. Fixing these two in `swarm/` and the submitter overlaps with what ksiox is changing right now, so it would be better agreed with them first.

My suggestion: send ksiox `41f7fc5` and `e76aad5` to merge into `main`, and agree with them who takes the start freeze and the submit timeouts.

content.text:
It's going well so far:

- **ERP:** all five requirements (A-1 to A-5) are being searched in parallel, about one minute into the run. Our swarm needed 5–7 minutes to reach this point.
- **Stroke:** the agent searched with the real usable stroke, 576 against a nominal 600. That means it already has the end reserve from the technical-release mail, which our runs often missed.
- **Bid form:** the submit agent is already opening the tender, so filling the form starts early.

There's one weak spot. A few searches typed into the search box but it stayed empty ("field shows ''"). The agents retry with the catalogue group and find the materials, but it costs a step each time.

# Pilot runtime: bugs seen in sandbox runs

One section per test run of this branch. Values from the scenario (material numbers, references, receipt numbers,
prices, message ids) are deliberately left out: the full logs live in the git-ignored `.swarm/runs/<run>-log.md` of
whoever pulled them (`scripts/pull-run.ps1 <run>` or `atira logs <run>`).

## run_88a2457dba119ab0 (b4a6251, public dataset, 2026-10-11)

Start was fast: all four sites past cookies/gates within ~20 s, spec read at 0:45, tender documents at 0:59, ERP
searches running in parallel per requirement from ~0:50. After round 0 (~4:00) the bid had 5 positions, **0 priced,
0 with a material**, discount still 0 %. The problems below are why.

### 1. Gate replay storm resets the mail search form (blocks all mail topics)
- `pilot/tab.py` `Tab.view()` / `_matching_recipe()`: every `observe` on the mail site replays the learned slider +
  checkbox recipe (157 `pilot.tab mail: replayed ...` lines in ~3 min, often 3-4 per second from parallel topic tabs).
- The webmail re-locks the slider after each search and re-renders the form; the replay then fires again, and the
  search text the model just typed is gone: `fill #N='<reference> <topic>': field shows ''` (8+ times), followed by
  "Keine Nachrichten gefunden" and "SAME actions ... try something else".
- Result: 7 of 8 mail topic agents hit their 8-step limit with `done=False`; technical release, price indices and
  project bonus saved 0 pages. Only the setup-pool topic finished.
- Fix idea: do not replay a gate recipe while the page still shows the control state the recipe itself produces after
  the last search (same rule as `swarm/guard.py` 54fefd1 "leave a gate alone once it shows the status it had after
  our own fill"), and never replay between a model `fill` and its `click` in the same step.

### 2. ERP agents keep acting on a closed page (no recovery)
- Two requirement agents: `goto ...: navigation error: Page.goto: Target page, context or browser has been closed`
  repeated for 6-8 steps until the step limit; `click: 'no control #7 on the current view'` in between.
- Trigger: the F4 search help opens in a new tab / the page the agent held was closed under it.
- Fix idea: in the navigator, on "has been closed" replace `tab.page` with the newest open page of the context (or a
  new page at `site.home`) and re-observe instead of passing the error back to the model.

### 3. ERP search field does not take the first fill
- `fill #5='<catalogue group>': field shows ''` on the first try in 4 of 5 requirement agents; a second identical try
  works. Costs 1-2 of 14 steps per agent. One agent typed all requirement attributes as one search string first.
- Fix idea: after a fill that reads back empty, focus + type (`keyboard.type`) once before reporting failure; tell the
  model the search help takes one term (the catalogue group).

### 4. ERP agents guess record URLs
- One agent read invented paths (`/material?no=...`, `/price?no=...`): 404 pages saved as evidence, 4 times in a row.
- Fix idea: drop saved pages whose title/body is a 404; in the ERP goal, only follow hrefs present on the page.

### 5. Step limits end ERP work before the record tabs
- All five `Erp[...]` agents stopped at 14 steps with `done=False` after saving only the search list and the basic
  data tab; status, lead times, prices and stock were never read, so no position got a material (round 0: 0/5).
- Fix idea: the runtime should start follow-up jobs per candidate material (record tabs, VK13 scales, MMBE) instead of
  one long job per requirement; a step limit with `done=False` must leave a gap the next round picks up.

### 6. Tender Q&A not found
- `TenderReader` spent steps 8-14 re-clicking the same procedure-file dropdown ("SAME actions" twice) and ended at the
  step limit without the bidder Q&A, so quantity changes and the withdrawn-answer check are missing.
- Fix idea: when a dropdown click changes nothing, list the links/tabs on the page (the Q&A tab is a link inside the
  dropdown) or open the dropdown entries by href.

### 7. Mail topic agents read the wrong message
- The condition-rules agent searched the bare reference, opened the discount approval and saved it as its topic.
- The FX agent opened the look-alike message first and ran out of steps before the valid one.
- DiscountAnalyzer stayed at `0/1`, `0/2 valid messages` although the valid approval page was saved several times:
  the reading-pane content was not in the saved text ("message content is not visible in the frame").
- Fix idea: save the message's own page (`/messages/<id>`) rather than the list page with the reading pane; open
  candidates newest-first and skip subjects with a suffix after the exact reference.

### 8. Minor
- ERP entry: `ElementHandle.fill: Timeout 4000ms exceeded` on the receipt field (second try worked).
- `click #N: skipped (page changed)` after a click that navigated: the second planned action is dropped silently.
- The platform's input log shows two searches typed back to back in one browser (`"<a><b>"`); possibly only the
  recorder merging parallel tabs, but worth checking that parallel topic tabs never share one page/focus.

content.text:
I logged the bugs on `claude/funny-allen-z0iuyw` in a new file, `docs/PILOT-BUGS.md`, and pushed it as commit `8e80462`.

The raw logs did not go into the branch. Anything committed there gets packed into the sandbox package, and the logs contain scenario values (material numbers, references, receipt numbers, message ids), which the fair-play rules forbid. The full log is kept locally, outside git, in `.swarm/runs/run_88a2457dba119ab0-log.md`, and the monitor keeps adding to it until the run ends. The bug file describes each problem without those values.

**Logged bugs**, worst first. At about 4 minutes in, the pilot had 0 of 5 positions with a material or price, and a 0% discount.

1. **The mail search box keeps getting wiped.** The pilot re-runs the mail page's unlock steps (slider and checkbox) on every page check, 157 times in about 3 minutes. That reloads the search form and clears what the model just typed. 7 of the 8 mail topics hit their step limit without finishing.
2. **ERP agents keep working on a closed page.** "Target page has been closed" repeated for 6–8 steps with no recovery.
3. **The ERP search box doesn't take the first entry.** Agents type the search term, the box stays empty, and they must retry.
4. **ERP agents guess record URLs.** The resulting 404 pages get saved as evidence.
5. **Step limits end ERP work too early.** Agents stop after the search list, before status, lead time, prices and stock.
6. **The tender agent never found the bidder Q&A.** It kept clicking the same dropdown.
7. **Mail agents read the wrong message, and the discount is never found.** The condition-rules agent saved the discount approval as its topic. The FX agent opened the look-alike message first. The discount analyzer stayed at 0 valid messages because the message text wasn't in the saved page.
8. **The follow-up ERP job had no search terms.** Its goal named only the position numbers, so it searched the material help for "01.01".
9. **Minor:** one fill timeout, a second planned action silently dropped after a page change, and two searches that look typed back to back into one browser.

Each bug lists where it happens in the code and a suggested fix. The run is still going; when it finishes I'll add the final outcome and score to the same file.

content.text:
The pilot run (run_88a2) scored **10**. It signed an empty bid at 5:47, with about 14 of its 20 minutes still unused.

- **What scored:** the decision ("bid") and the tender reference.
- **What was entered:** no positions, discount 0%, net total 0.
- **Cost:** very low, $0.066 and 263 model calls, so the new runtime is fast.

The problem is that the bid form was released and signed before any data had come in. By then the ERP agents had matched no material, and the follow-up ERP job had searched the material catalogue for the position numbers ("01.01") instead of any real attributes.

I added this as bug 0 (the worst) to `docs/PILOT-BUGS.md` on `claude/funny-allen-z0iuyw`, along with the final result. The latest commit there is `71451d2`.

The suggested fix: never sign a bid with no priced positions before the collection deadline. The form can wait on the summary page and request the signing code (TAN) only at the end.

The full log and the run summary are local only, in `.swarm/runs/`, and the run is recorded in `INDEX.md`.
